question: The rule for how a design has to account for its screens has changed several times. What does it require now?
answer: Under 093 FR-014 as restated by 2026-08-14-a-screen-has-a-name, a design whose visual declaration carries shape="screens" must name every screen the declared material holds, and every named screen must resolve to a screen in that material. A screen present but not named, and a name that resolves to nothing, are each reported as an error naming the screen and the design. The named set is the authority for what the feature claims, and the material is read only to check that claim, never to derive it. FR-015 supplies the means: a declaration can name its screens by each screen's own identifier.

question: How did the list of categories that profile enforcement detects change between 10 and 12 July 2026?
answer: It grew from six categories (formatter, linter, type-checker, security, supply-chain, test-runner) to nine. Coverage was added, detected only from a declared threshold or check (fail_under, a coverageThreshold block, a JaCoCo check rule), never a bare coverage library, and never presented as proof of a CI diff-gate. Observability was added, detected from a deliberately named metrics registry, exporter or starter dependency, not a transitive core or tracing-only package, and never presented as proof that /metrics is wired. Contract-first was added, detected from a checked-in interface contract (OpenAPI/Swagger, *.proto, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI; JSON Schema only under contracts/) and gated on an exposed interface per FR-014. The changelog dates all three to 11 Jul; git records them on 12 Jul UTC, in the order coverage, observability, contract-first.

question: Between v0.1.0-pre.25 and v0.1.0-pre.26, what did spec 105 add about the token candidates an import pulls out of a design export?
answer: One change, 2026-08-22-what-a-candidate-is-made-of, applied 22 Aug 2026, which bounded derivation's output for the first time. A candidate must carry which kind of value it is. Colour derivation must recognise hexadecimal plus the functional notations rgb(), rgba(), hsl(), hsla(), hwb(), lab(), lch(), oklab(), oklch() and color(). Spacing derivation must recognise only lengths declared on a spacing property (padding, margin, gap, inset and their longhands) and must not present lengths declared anywhere else. Suppressing already-declared values must compare against every form the declared token set records, and must not attempt equality across colour spaces. The rationale: code had chosen hex-only colour, so an oklch() export derived nothing, and no spacing derivation existed at all.
